13.example: Archaeologists study artifacts to understand the daily life of ancient people.

13.english_meaning: The aggregate of people living together in a more or less ordered community.

13.english_meaning: A new printed edition of a book, document, or text.

13.english_meaning: The stage of human social and cultural development and organization that is considered most advanced.

13.example: Babylon was a major ancient city located near the Euphrates River.

13.english_meaning: The study of past events, particularly in human affairs.
13.example: Written records mark the beginning of recorded history.

13.english_meaning: An area or division, especially part of a country or the world having definable characteristics.

13.english_meaning: A book used as a standard work for the study of a particular subject.
13.example: NCERT publishes this history textbook for senior secondary students.

14.english_meaning: People who study human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts and other physical remains.

14.english_meaning: To build or create something again, or to form an impression, idea, or story about a past event from available evidence.
14.example: Historians use old records and artifacts to reconstruct the lives of ancient people.

14.english_meaning: The fact or state of living or having objective reality.
14.example: The origins of human existence can be traced back millions of years.

14.english_meaning: Far away in space or time.
14.example: Scientists study the remote past to learn about early human ancestors.

14.english_meaning: A place giving temporary protection from bad weather or danger.
14.example: Early humans lived in natural caves and rock shelters.

14.english_meaning: The action of collecting or bringing together wild fruits, vegetables, or other items.
14.example: Early societies survived by hunting animals and gathering plant produce.

14.english_meaning: An ancient region in the eastern Mediterranean, corresponding to modern-day Iraq.
14.example: Some of the earliest cities developed in Mesopotamia.

14.english_meaning: A very large quantity of something; plentifulness.
14.example: Archaeologists found an abundance of written material in the ancient ruins.

14.english_meaning: People who practiced writing down documents, laws, and records before the widespread use of printing.
14.example: Scribes played a crucial role in maintaining administrative records in early cities.

14.english_meaning: Relating to the keeping or grazing of sheep or cattle.
14.example: Pastoral people played an important trading role in many ancient towns.

14.english_meaning: The action of establishing an organization, institution, or town.
14.example: Several developments took place long before the establishment of the first cities.

14.english_meaning: Likely to have a great and important effect or influence.

14.english_meaning: Taking place or progressing slowly, step by step.

14.english_meaning: The science or practice of farming, including cultivation of the soil and rearing of animals.

14.english_meaning: The available body of facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true.

14.english_meaning: A building devoted to the worship, or regarded as the dwelling place, of a god or gods.

15.example: The adoption of agriculture changed human life from a nomadic to a settled lifestyle.

15.english_meaning: To tame (an animal) or cultivate (a plant) for human use.
15.example: Early humans learned to domesticate animals like sheep, goats, and cattle for milk and meat.

15.english_meaning: A hardy cereal grain that is used for food, livestock feed, and brewing.
15.example: Wheat and barley were among the first crops grown in West Asia.

15.english_meaning: A type of grain grown widely as a cereal crop in dry regions.

15.example: Peas and various kinds of pulses were grown along with wheat in West Asia.

15.english_meaning: A thread or filament from which a vegetable tissue, mineral substance, or textile is formed.

15.example: Stone axes and hoes were used to clear land and cultivate crops.

15.english_meaning: Characteristic of one person or thing, so as to distinguish it from others.
15.example: Copper ores were collected and used for their distinctive bluish-green colour.

15.english_meaning: After a particular thing has happened; afterward.
15.example: This prepared the way for the extensive use of metal subsequently.

15.english_meaning: A dark, glass-like volcanic rock formed by the rapid solidification of lava.
15.hindi_meaning: एक प्रकार का कांच जैसा ज्वालामुखी पत्थर
15.example: Precious stones and obsidian were traded from distant lands.

15.english_meaning: A result or effect of an action or condition.
15.example: The agricultural developments had far-reaching consequences for early human society.

15.english_meaning: Relating to the study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts.
15.example: Archaeological discoveries help us understand how early communities lived and migrated.

16.english_meaning: A fundamental and relatively sudden change in political power and organizational structures or a dramatic and wide-reaching change in conditions.
16.example: The invention of agriculture brought a major revolution in human history.

16.english_meaning: Made a thorough or dramatic change in the form, appearance, or character of something.
16.hindi_meaning: रूपांतरित या पूरी तरह बदला हुआ
16.example: New technologies have transformed the way we communicate today.

16.english_meaning: The unbroken and consistent existence or operation of something over a period of time.
16.example: Historians study both the changes and continuities in ancient civilizations.

16.english_meaning: Differing strikingly, especially in color, tone, or character.
16.example: The two brothers had contrasting views on how to manage the business.

16.english_meaning: The aggregate of people living together in a more or less ordered community.
16.example: Ancient societies depended heavily on river valleys for survival.

16.english_meaning: The activity or business of growing crops and raising livestock.
16.example: Farming allowed humans to settle down in permanent villages.

16.english_meaning: A group of people living in the same place or having a particular characteristic in common.

16.english_meaning: Associated with or relating to livestock farming or the keeping of grazing animals.
16.example: Pastoral peoples moved from place to place in search of fresh pastures for their flocks.

16.english_meaning: Members of a particular nation, community, or ethnic group.
16.example: The indigenous peoples of the region have a deep understanding of nature.

16.english_meaning: Members of a nomadic people who live chiefly by hunting, fishing, and harvesting wild food.
16.hindi_meaning: शिकारी-संग्रहकर्ता (जो शिकार और कंदमूल इकट्ठा करके जीते हैं)

16.english_meaning: Inhabitants or persons who live in a specified place.
16.example: City dwellers faced different challenges compared to rural farmers.

16.english_meaning: A graphic representation of the passage of time as a line.

16.english_meaning: Subjects or topics of a discourse or of a artistic or literary composition.
16.example: This book explores four major themes in world history.

16.english_meaning: Including or providing a great deal of information.
16.example: The scientist gave a detailed explanation of the archaeological find.

16.english_meaning: The action of traveling in or through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it.
16.example: Space exploration has advanced rapidly over the last century.

16.english_meaning: Identification of someone or something or appreciation of validity.
16.example: Her contributions to history brought her global recognition.

16.english_meaning: Separated by a distance, or excluding/aside from.

16.english_meaning: Slight or indirect indications or suggestions.
16.example: The teacher gave us a few hints to solve the puzzle.

17.english_meaning: A display of a list of events in chronological order.
17.example: The history textbook includes a detailed timeline of ancient civilizations.

17.english_meaning: The process of coming into view or becoming prominent.
17.example: The emergence of human speech changed the course of history.

17.english_meaning: The process of taming an animal and keeping it as a pet or on a farm, or cultivating plants.
17.example: The domestication of plants and animals marked the beginning of agriculture.
The use of fire and metal tools were major technological advances.

17.english_meaning: The science or practice of farming, including cultivation of the soil and rearing of animals.
17.example: Plough agriculture allowed early societies to produce surplus food.

17.english_meaning: An extensive group of states or countries ruled over by a single monarch or a sovereign state.
17.example: The timeline mentions the establishment of some of the earliest empires.

17.english_meaning: The action or process of maturing or developing fully.
17.example: A date on the timeline may indicate when a historical process reaches maturation.

17.english_meaning: An expert in or student of history.

17.english_meaning: The available body of facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true.

17.english_meaning: Serving as a sign or indication of something.

18.english_meaning: A place giving temporary protection from bad weather or danger.
18.hindi_meaning: मौसम या खतरे से सुरक्षा प्रदान करने वाला स्थान या आश्रय (जैसे गुफाएँ)।

18.english_meaning: Relating to the Mediterranean Sea or the countries surrounding it.

18.hindi_meaning: जीवों या मानव जाति का क्रमिक विकास या उद्भव (विकासवाद)।

20.english_meaning: The process of developing or being developed, leading to growth or advancement.
20.example: The development of a writing script was crucial for administration.

20.english_meaning: Plural of millennium; a period of a thousand years.
20.example: Human societies evolved significantly over several millennia.

20.english_meaning: The action or process of adapting or being adapted to new conditions.
20.example: Survival in harsh climates required constant cultural and physical adaptation.

20.english_meaning: A particular period of time in history or a person's life.
20.example: This historical epoch marks the transition from hunter-gatherers to settled farmers.

21.english_meaning: An advanced state of human society containing highly developed forms of culture, government, industry, and social levels.
21.example: Mesopotamian civilisation is known for its prosperity, city life, and rich literature.

21.english_meaning: The state of being successful economically or financially; good fortune and wealth.
21.example: The ancient kingdom achieved great prosperity through trade and agriculture.

21.english_meaning: Occupying or containing much space; very lengthy or large in volume or writing.
21.example: The library contained voluminous records written on clay tablets.

21.english_meaning: The branch of science that studies celestial bodies, space, and the physical universe as a whole.
21.example: Ancient Mesopotamians made significant advancements in mathematics and astronomy.

21.english_meaning: The way a thing turns out; a consequence, result, or effect.
21.example: We shall explore the outcomes of a sustained tradition of writing.

21.english_meaning: Continuing for a long time without interruption or weakening.
21.example: Sustained efforts in archaeological research revealed hidden ancient cities.

21.english_meaning: Made suitable for towns or cities; characterized by the growth of towns and cities.
21.example: The southern region of Mesopotamia became highly urbanised over time.

21.english_meaning: Grew or developed in a healthy or vigorous way, especially as the result of a particularly favorable environment.
21.example: The Akkadian language flourished till about Alexander’s time.

21.english_meaning: The study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts and other physical remains.
21.example: Archaeology in Mesopotamia began in the 1840s with extensive excavations.

21.english_meaning: The action of excavating something, especially an archaeological site.
21.example: At sites like Uruk and Mari, excavations continued for decades.

21.english_meaning: Things used to make something look more attractive but usually having no practical purpose, such as jewelry.
21.example: Archaeologists found numerous statues, ornaments, and graves at the site.

21.english_meaning: A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence.
21.example: Thousands of written documents were discovered in the ancient ruins.

21.english_meaning: Inherited from or belonging to one's ancestors or forebears.
21.example: European scholars looked at Mesopotamia as a kind of ancestral land.

21.english_meaning: Taking words in their usual or most basic sense without metaphor or exaggeration.
21.example: There was an attempt to prove the literal truth of the Old Testament.

21.english_meaning: Obtained or sourced from a specified origin or root word.
21.example: The name Mesopotamia is derived from Greek words.

21.english_meaning: A state in which supreme power is held by the people and their elected president or leader rather than a monarch.
21.example: The ancient land of Mesopotamia is now part of the Republic of Iraq.

21.english_meaning: A specialist in a particular branch of study, especially the humanities; an academic person.
21.example: Travellers and scholars of Europe studied ancient Mesopotamian texts extensively.

21.english_meaning: The action of mentioning or alluding to something or someone.
21.example: Mesopotamia was important to Europeans because of references to it in the Old Testament.

22.english_meaning: An ancient region in the Tigris-Euphrates river system, broadly corresponding to modern-day Iraq.
22.hindi_meaning: दजला और फरात नदियों की घाटी की प्राचीन सभ्यता (आधुनिक इराक क्षेत्र)।
22.example: Mesopotamia is often called the cradle of civilization.

22.english_meaning: A journey undertaken by a group of people for a specific purpose, especially that of exploration.
22.hindi_meaning: विशेष उद्देश्य या अन्वेषण के लिए की जाने वाली यात्रा (अभियान)।
22.example: The museum funded an archaeological expedition to find ancient tablets.

22.english_meaning: Relating to the study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts.
22.example: Advanced archaeological techniques help us understand ancient lifestyles.

22.english_meaning: Developed to a high degree of complexity; advanced.
22.example: Modern scientists use sophisticated equipment to analyze ancient artifacts.

22.english_meaning: Spoken or written accounts of connected events; stories.
22.example: The biblical narratives often contain deep historical memories.

22.english_meaning: Went back or further away; became fainter or less important.
22.hindi_meaning: पीछे हटना या कम महत्वपूर्ण हो जाना।
22.example: The literal truth of the myth receded into the background of modern research.

22.english_meaning: After a particular event or time; afterward.
22.hindi_meaning: तदनंतर, बाद में या इसके परिणामस्वरूप।
22.example: Much of what we discuss subsequently is based on these studies.

22.english_meaning: The transmission of customs or beliefs from generation to generation.
22.example: The Mesopotamian tradition shares similarities with the story of Noah.

22.english_meaning: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives.
22.example: Iraq is a land of diverse geographical environments.

22.english_meaning: Having a smoothly rising and falling form or outline; wave-like.
22.hindi_meaning: लहरदार या ऊपर-नीचे ढाल वाली भूमि।
22.example: Green, undulating plains characterize the north-eastern part of the region.

22.english_meaning: The science or practice of farming, including cultivation of the soil and rearing of livestock.
22.example: Agriculture began in the north-eastern plains between 7000 and 6000 BCE.

22.english_meaning: A large, flat area of uncultivated grassland, particularly in Siberia or southeast Europe and Asia.
22.hindi_meaning: घास का मैदान या स्टेपी (शुष्क घास क्षेत्र)।
22.example: In the northern upland steppe, animal herding is common.

22.english_meaning: A means of securing the necessities of life.
22.example: Animal herding offers people a better livelihood in the steppe region.

22.english_meaning: Rivers or streams flowing into a larger river or lake.
22.example: Tributaries of the Tigris provide important routes for travel and trade.

22.english_meaning: People living together in a more or less ordered community.
22.example: Many ancient societies have myths about catastrophic floods.

22.english_meaning: Maintaining something in its original or existing state.
22.hindi_meaning: संरक्षित करना या बचा कर रखना।
22.example: Oral myths were a way of preserving historical memories.

22.english_meaning: Stood for or symbolized something; portrayed in a particular way.
22.hindi_meaning: चित्रित किया गया, दर्शाया गया या प्रतिनिधित्व किया गया।
22.example: Life before and after the flood is represented through traditional stories.

22.english_meaning: Intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval.
22.example: There was great enthusiasm for exploring the ancient past of Mesopotamia.

23.english_meaning: The imparting or exchanging of information or means of sending messages.
23.example: The difficult terrain made communication into the mountains of Iran very challenging.

23.english_meaning: To come forth into view or out of a state or place; to arise.
23.example: This is where the first cities and writing emerged in the southern desert.

23.english_meaning: Fine sand, clay, or other material carried by running water and deposited as a sediment.
23.example: The rivers Euphrates and Tigris carry loads of fertile silt that enrich the soil.

23.english_meaning: To lay down or let fall (a substance) as a layer or sediment.
23.example: When the rivers flood, fertile silt is deposited on the surrounding fields.

23.english_meaning: Bands or passages through which water or other liquids flow.
23.example: After entering the desert, the river water flows out into small channels.

23.english_meaning: The supply of water to land or crops to help growth, typically by means of channels.
23.example: These water channels functioned as irrigation canals for the crops.

23.english_meaning: A hardy cereal grain that has coarse bristles, widely used in brewing and for livestock feed.
23.example: Farmers in ancient Mesopotamia grew wheat, barley, peas, and lentils.

23.english_meaning: A high-protein edible seed of a cultivated plant of the legume family, used as food.
23.example: Lentils were among the staple crops cultivated along the river valleys.

23.english_meaning: producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.
23.example: The agriculture of southern Mesopotamia was exceptionally productive.
The region did not have sufficient rainfall to grow crops naturally.

23.english_meaning: Of cattle, sheep, etc., to eat grass in a field.
23.example: Sheep and goats grazed on the steppe and mountain slopes.

23.english_meaning: A large, flat area of land with grass and few trees, especially in Eastern Europe and Asia.
23.example: Mesopotamian sheep and goats were fed on the open steppe.

23.english_meaning: Surfaces of a mountain or hill that are inclined from a horizontal or vertical line.
23.example: Animals grazed on the mountain slopes which were too high for floods to reach.

23.english_meaning: Areas of land, typically a large one.
23.example: These tracts of land were too high for the rivers to flood and fertilise.

23.english_meaning: A very large quantity of something; plentifulness.
23.example: Meat, milk, and wool were produced in abundance.

23.english_meaning: The state of being successful, usually by making a lot of money or having good living conditions.
23.example: We should not think that cities grew simply because of rural prosperity.

23.english_meaning: Elements or circumstances contributing to a particular result.
23.example: We shall discuss other important factors later in the chapter.

23.english_meaning: Supplied with water by artificial means such as canals or ditches.
23.example: The map highlights the irrigated zone of southern Mesopotamia.

24.english_meaning: The lifestyle and characteristic way of life in cities and towns, involving non-agricultural economic activities.
24.hindi_meaning: नगरीकरण (शहरों की जीवनशैली और कृषि के अलावा अन्य आर्थिक गतिविधियों का विकास)
24.example: The significance of urbanism lies in the development of trade, manufactures, and specialized services.

24.english_meaning: The system of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a region.
24.hindi_meaning: अर्थव्यवस्था (वस्तुओं और सेवाओं के उत्पादन, वितरण और उपभोग की प्रणाली)
24.example: An urban economy comprises trade, manufacturing, and various public services.

24.english_meaning: To consist of, make up, or include various parts or elements.
24.hindi_meaning: शामिल होना या से मिलकर बनना
24.example: Urban economies comprise not only food production but also trade and manufactures.

24.english_meaning: Needing no outside help in satisfying one's basic needs; independent.
24.hindi_meaning: आत्मनिर्भर (अपनी आवश्यकताओं के लिए दूसरों पर निर्भर न रहने वाला)
24.example: City people cease to be self-sufficient and depend on the products and services of others.

24.english_meaning: Concentration on a particular activity, skill, or field of study.
24.hindi_meaning: विशेषीकरण (किसी एक कार्य या कला में विशेष दक्षता प्राप्त करना)
24.example: His specialisation is fine stone carving, not trading or making tools.

24.english_meaning: The assignment of different parts of a manufacturing process or task to different people in order to improve efficiency.
24.hindi_meaning: श्रम विभाजन (कार्यों को अलग-अलग लोगों के बीच विभाजित करना)
24.example: The division of labour is a fundamental mark of complex urban life.

24.english_meaning: The patterned set of relationships and institutions that shape a society.
24.example: A proper social organisation is required to manage fuel, metal, and food storage in cities.

24.english_meaning: Organized and managed so that different elements work well together.
24.example: Many different activities have to be coordinated to keep the city functioning smoothly.

24.english_meaning: Carved, molded, or fashioned out of a hard material like stone or wood.
24.hindi_meaning: तर्कषित या तराशा हुआ (मूर्ति या कलाकृति बनाना)
24.example: This woman's head was sculpted in white marble at Uruk before 3000 BCE.

24.english_meaning: Pieces of material embedded into a surface to decorate it.
24.hindi_meaning: जड़ाऊ काम (सजावट के लिए सतह के अंदर जड़े गए टुकड़े)
24.example: The eyes and eyebrows of the sculpture featured lapis lazuli and shell inlays.

24.english_meaning: A long, narrow cut or depression in a hard surface.
24.example: There is a groove along the top of the head, perhaps for attaching an ornament.

24.english_meaning: The action of obtaining or acquiring something, especially with effort.
24.hindi_meaning: प्राप्ति या अधिप्राप्ति (किसी वस्तु को जुटाना या प्राप्त करना)
24.example: Beginning with the procurement of stone, list all the specialists involved in production.

24.english_meaning: A metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength.
24.hindi_meaning: मिश्र धातु (दो या दो से अधिक धातुओं का मिश्रण)
24.example: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

24.english_meaning: The activity or occupation of making or repairing wooden objects and structures.
24.example: Metal tools were necessary for accurate carpentry and drilling beads.

24.english_meaning: A bright blue semiprecious stone valued for ornamentation.
24.hindi_meaning: लाजवर्द (एक गहरे नीले रंग का मूल्यवान पत्थर)
24.example: The eyes of the Warka head would probably have taken blue lapis lazuli.

24.english_meaning: A black, sticky, tar-like petroleum substance used for sealing or binding.
24.hindi_meaning: कोलतार या डामर (एक प्रकार का काला चिपचिपा पदार्थ)
24.example: The eyebrows of the sculpture were inlaid with black bitumen.

24.english_meaning: The art or technique of representing or shaping a figure or object.
24.example: The sculpture is admired for the delicate modelling of the woman’s mouth and chin.

24.english_meaning: Bring goods or materials into a country or region from abroad for use or sale.
24.hindi_meaning: आयातित (दूर किसी अन्य स्थान से मंगवाया गया)
24.example: The hard stone used for the sculpture would have been imported from a distance.

25.english_meaning: Natural substances found in the earth, such as metals, stones, and ores.
25.example: The southern region lacked mineral resources like stone and metal.

25.english_meaning: To guess or infer that something is true without having definite proof.
25.example: We can surmise that ancient traders exchanged textiles for timber and metals.

25.english_meaning: Existing or available in large quantities; overflowing.
25.example: Mesopotamia had abundant agricultural produce to trade with other regions.

25.english_meaning: Types of cloth or woven fabric.
25.example: Mesopotamians traded their abundant textiles for foreign resources.

25.english_meaning: Journeys undertaken by a group for a specific purpose, such as trade or exploration.
25.example: The rulers equipped foreign expeditions to secure timber and metals.
Without cheap transportation, the city economy would not be viable.

25.english_meaning: Long, flat-bottomed boats used for carrying heavy loads on rivers or canals.
25.hindi_meaning: बार्ज (नदी में माल ढोने वाली सपाट नाव)
25.example: Barges loaded with sacks of grain sailed down the Euphrates river.

25.english_meaning: Driven, pushed, or moved forward in a particular direction.
25.example: River boats are propelled by the current of the river and the wind.

25.english_meaning: Lengths of water wider than a strait, often man-made for navigation or irrigation.
25.example: Natural channels and canals served as important transport routes in ancient Mesopotamia.

25.english_meaning: Places where people have established a community and built homes.
25.example: Goods were transported between large and small settlements through canals.

25.english_meaning: The sharing of information using spoken or written words.
25.example: All societies have languages for verbal communication.

25.english_meaning: A writing system consisting of different characters or signs.
25.example: The cuneiform script represented spoken sounds in visible signs.

25.english_meaning: Flat pieces of clay used in ancient times for writing records.
25.example: The first Mesopotamian clay tablets contained picture-like signs.

25.english_meaning: Handed out or shared among a group of people.
25.example: Goods were brought into or distributed from the temples of Uruk.

25.english_meaning: Business exchanges or records of goods given and received.
25.example: Society needed writing to keep accurate records of economic transactions.

25.english_meaning: Wedge-shaped characters used in the ancient writing systems of Mesopotamia.
25.example: Cuneiform syllabic signs were inscribed on clay using a wedge-shaped stylus.

25.english_meaning: Relating to or consisting of syllables representing units of sound.
25.example: The script evolved into cuneiform syllabic signs over time.

25.english_meaning: Written or carved words or symbols on a surface.
25.example: Symbols and numbers were inscribed on wet clay tablets.

26.english_meaning: An ancient region in the Middle East situated between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, often called the cradle of civilization.
26.hindi_meaning: दजला और फ़ुरात नदियों के बीच स्थित प्राचीन मध्य-पूर्व का क्षेत्र, जिसे सभ्यता का पालना कहा जाता है।
26.example: Mesopotamia is known for being one of the first places to develop writing and cities.

26.english_meaning: A person who copies out documents, especially one employed in the ancient world before the invention of printing.
26.hindi_meaning: लिपिक या लेखक; प्राचीन काल में ताड़पत्रों या मिट्टी की तख्तियों पर लिखने वाला व्यक्ति।
26.example: The royal scribe carefully recorded the king's new laws on a clay tablet.

26.english_meaning: In a slanted or diagonal direction; not in a direct, straight, or perpendicular way.
26.hindi_meaning: तिरछे रूप से या कोण बनाते हुए।
26.example: He cut the reed obliquely to create a sharp edge for writing.

26.english_meaning: Denoting or relating to the wedge-shaped characters used in the ancient writing systems of Mesopotamia.
26.hindi_meaning: मेसोपोटामिया की प्राचीन कील के आकार की (कीलानुमा) लिपि।
26.example: Archaeologists deciphered the ancient cuneiform script on the clay tablets.

26.english_meaning: Not able to be destroyed; extremely durable and long-lasting.
26.hindi_meaning: जो आसानी से नष्ट न हो सके, अविनाशकारी या टिकाऊ।
26.example: Once baked in the sun, the clay tablets became almost indestructible.

26.english_meaning: An instance of buying or selling something; a business deal or exchange.
26.example: Every commercial transaction required a separate written record in ancient Mesopotamia.

26.english_meaning: Existing, occurring, or living at the same time; belonging to the same period.
26.hindi_meaning: समकालीन; उसी काल या समय का।
26.example: We know much more about Mesopotamia than we do about contemporary India.

26.english_meaning: The language of ancient Sumer, the earliest known language of Mesopotamia.
26.hindi_meaning: सुमेर की भाषा, जो मेसोपोटामिया की सबसे पुरानी ज्ञात भाषा थी।
26.example: By 2600 BCE, the official language of writing in southern Mesopotamia was Sumerian.

26.english_meaning: An extinct Semitic language of ancient Mesopotamia that gradually replaced Sumerian.
26.hindi_meaning: अक्कादियन भाषा; प्राचीन मेसोपोटामिया की एक भाषा जिसने धीरे-धीरे सुमेरियन का स्थान ले लिया।
26.example: Cuneiform writing in the Akkadian language continued for over two thousand years.

26.english_meaning: The state of being legally or officially acceptable and binding.
26.hindi_meaning: वैधता; कानूनी या आधिकारिक रूप से मान्य होने की स्थिति।
26.example: Writing was used for giving legal validity to land transfers.

26.english_meaning: According to the customs or usual practices of a society.
26.hindi_meaning: प्रथागत या परंपरा के अनुसार होने वाला।
26.example: The king announced changes in the customary laws of the land.

26.english_meaning: A basic speech sound in which the breath is at least partly obstructed.
26.hindi_meaning: वर्णमाला का व्यंजन वर्ण (स्वर के अलावा अन्य ध्वनि)।
26.example: The cuneiform sign did not represent a single consonant like 'm'.

26.english_meaning: A speech sound which is produced by an open passage of the vocal tract.
26.hindi_meaning: स्वर वर्ण (जैसे a, e, i, o, u)।
26.example: In English, 'a' and 'e' are important vowels.

26.english_meaning: A unit of pronunciation having one vowel sound, with or without surrounding consonants, forming the whole or a part of a word.
26.example: The cuneiform signs represented syllables rather than single letters.

26.english_meaning: Relating to the study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts.
26.hindi_meaning: पुरातत्वीय; प्राचीन अवशेषों और स्थलों की खुदाई से संबंधित।
26.example: Thousands of clay tablets were discovered at various Mesopotamian archaeological sites.

26.english_meaning: The side of a coin or medal bearing the principal design or inscription; the front side.
26.hindi_meaning: किसी वस्तु या तख्ती का सामने का भाग या पृष्ठ।
26.example: You can see a triangle on the top of the obverse side of the clay tablet.

26.english_meaning: The stage of human social and cultural development and organization that is considered most advanced.
26.hindi_meaning: सभ्यता; मानव समाज और संस्कृति के विकास का उन्नत चरण।
26.example: Mesopotamia is regarded as one of the earliest river-valley civilisations.

26.english_meaning: An abundance of valuable possessions or money, or in this context, a large amount of something.
26.example: Because of this wealth of sources, we know a lot about ancient Mesopotamia.

27.english_meaning: An activity involving skill in making things by hand.
27.example: Pottery is an ancient craft practiced in many villages.

27.english_meaning: Relating to the ability to think and understand things logically.
27.example: Solving this complex puzzle required great intellectual effort.

27.english_meaning: A thing done successfully, typically by effort, courage, or skill.
27.example: Winning the science competition was a proud achievement for her.

27.english_meaning: Transporting or expressing a thought, feeling, or idea so that it is understood.
27.example: His paintings are successful in conveying deep emotions.

27.english_meaning: The ability to read and write.
27.example: The government launched new programs to improve rural literacy.

27.english_meaning: Words inscribed or carved on a monument, stone, or coin.
27.example: Historians studied the ancient inscriptions found on the temple walls.

27.english_meaning: Based on or occurring in myths; imaginary or legendary.
27.example: Dragons are mythical creatures found in many ancient stories.

27.english_meaning: The action of remembering something or keeping someone in mind.
27.example: A monument was built in remembrance of the brave soldiers.

27.english_meaning: A specialist in a particular branch of study, especially the humanities.
27.example: The scholar spent years translating ancient Sanskrit texts.

27.english_meaning: A relationship in which a person, thing, or idea is linked with another.
27.example: There is a strong connection between trade and the growth of cities.

27.english_meaning: A long poem, typically one derived from ancient oral tradition, narrating the deeds and adventures of heroic or legendary figures.
27.example: The Mahabharata is an ancient epic known worldwide.

27.english_meaning: The action of organizing something, or the structured arrangement of elements.
27.example: The successful organization of the event required careful planning.

27.english_meaning: A bright blue semi-precious stone used for decoration and jewelry in ancient times.
27.example: The king desired lapis lazuli to decorate the temple walls.

27.english_meaning: The process of making something more beautiful or attractive.
27.example: The town council started a project for the beautification of public parks.

27.english_meaning: A person who carries a message or goes on a message-bearing errand.
27.example: The king sent a trusted messenger to the neighboring kingdom.

27.english_meaning: Paid attention to; took notice of advice or instructions.
27.example: The driver heeded the warning sign and slowed down.

27.english_meaning: Greeted respectfully or acknowledged with a gesture of respect.
27.example: The soldiers saluted the commander as he walked past.

27.english_meaning: Finally; after a series of events or a long process.
27.example: After months of hard work, they ultimately achieved success.

28.english_meaning: Deduced or concluded from evidence and reasoning rather than from explicit statements.
28.example: It can be inferred from the poem that kingship organized trade and writing.

28.english_meaning: The position, office, or dignity of a king; royalty.
28.example: In Mesopotamian understanding, it was kingship that organized trade.

28.english_meaning: The process by which large numbers of people permanently concentrate in relatively small areas, forming cities.
28.example: Urbanisation in southern Mesopotamia began around 5000 BCE.

28.english_meaning: Places where people have set up a community to live, often newly established.
28.example: Early settlements in southern Mesopotamia gradually grew into cities.

28.english_meaning: Relating to an empire or an emperor.
28.example: Some of the early cities emerged as imperial cities.

118.hindi_meaning: कुलीन वर्गीय / अभिजात वर्ग से संबंधित
118.example: The aristocratic class held significant wealth and power during the medieval and early modern periods.

118.english_meaning: Believing that the Earth is the center of the universe or solar system (geocentric).
118.example: The church's earth-centric belief was eventually overturned by scientific discoveries.

118.english_meaning: The collection of planets and their moons orbiting around the sun.
118.example: Scientists began to understand the true nature of the solar system, replacing older beliefs.

118.english_meaning: Focusing on Europe and European culture to the exclusion of other cultures; eurocentric.
118.example: New geographical knowledge challenged the Europe-centric view of the world.

118.english_meaning: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.
118.example: Valuable historical documents and manuscripts are carefully preserved in archives.

118.english_meaning: The cultural revival that took place in Europe from the 14th to the 17th century, literally meaning 'rebirth'.
118.example: Historians used the term Renaissance to describe the sweeping cultural changes in Europe.

118.english_meaning: A specialist in a particular branch of study, especially the humanities.
118.example: Jacob Burckhardt was a prominent Swiss scholar of the nineteenth century.

118.english_meaning: Not content or happy with something; feeling that something is not as good as it should be.
118.example: Burckhardt was dissatisfied with the limited goals that his master had set for history writing.

118.english_meaning: The art or practice of designing and constructing buildings.
118.example: The book drew attention to literature, architecture, and painting to tell the story of the Renaissance.

118.english_meaning: Relating to a Renaissance cultural movement that turned away from medieval scholasticism and revived interest in ancient Greek and Roman thought.
118.example: A new humanist culture flowered in Italian towns during the fourteenth century.

118.english_meaning: The art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving or molding.
118.example: Museums across Europe contain countless ancient sculptures and paintings.

118.english_meaning: Types of cloth or woven fabric.
118.example: Historical material from the fourteenth century includes documents, paintings, and textiles.

118.english_meaning: Gave special importance to something in speaking or writing.
118.example: The historian who emphasised cultural changes most was Jacob Burckhardt.

118.english_meaning: Of chief importance; principal or most fundamental.
118.example: Ranke taught that the primary concern of a historian was to write about states and politics.

118.english_meaning: Abolished, invalidated, or reversed an established belief or system.
118.example: New scientific discoveries overturned the traditional earth-centric belief.

118.english_meaning: The transmission of customs or beliefs from generation to generation.
118.example: The chapter explores the changing cultural traditions of Europe from the fourteenth century.

119.english_meaning: Described or marked by peculiar features or qualities.
119.hindi_meaning: विशेषताओं से युक्त होना या लक्षण बताना
119.example: The era was characterised by a new belief in human potential.

119.english_meaning: A single human being as distinct from a group.
119.example: As an individual, man was capable of making his own decisions.

119.english_meaning: Relating to the Middle Ages in European history.
119.example: Medieval man's thinking was largely controlled by the church.

119.english_meaning: An improvement in the condition or strength of something.
119.example: The revival of Italian cities brought new cultural changes.

119.english_meaning: An extensive group of states or countries under a single supreme authority.
119.example: The fall of the western Roman Empire led to ruin in many towns.

119.english_meaning: Relating to the government or public affairs of a country.
119.example: Many towns that had been political centres fell into ruin.

119.english_meaning: Relating to the ideas, customs, and social behaviour of a society.
119.example: The region was a major cultural centre during the medieval period.

119.english_meaning: Made into a whole or made to act as a single unit.
119.example: There was no unified government in Italy at that time.
The Pope in Rome was sovereign in his own state.

119.english_meaning: Relating to the medieval system of lords, vassals, and land tenure.
119.example: Western Europe was being reshaped by feudal bonds.

119.english_meaning: Relating to the Eastern Roman Empire, centered in Constantinople.
119.example: Eastern Europe was unified under the Byzantine Empire.

119.english_meaning: Divided into parts or pieces; disunited.
119.example: During this period, Italy was weak and fragmented.

119.english_meaning: An event or instance of growth, progress, or change.
119.example: These very developments helped in the revival of Italian culture.

119.english_meaning: The action of becoming larger or more extensive.
119.example: With the expansion of trade, the ports on the Italian coast revived.

119.english_meaning: The stage of human social and cultural development and organization.
119.example: Islam was creating a common civilisation further west.

119.english_meaning: Nomadic people from Central Asia who built a vast empire.
119.example: The Mongols opened up trade with China via the Silk Route.

119.english_meaning: The transmission of customs or beliefs from generation to generation.
119.example: The textbook explores changing cultural traditions in Europe.

119.english_meaning: The state of being strikingly different from something else.
119.example: He was considered 'modern' in contrast to 'medieval' man.

120.english_meaning: A city that with its surrounding territory forms an independent state.
120.hindi_meaning: नगर-राज्य (एक स्वतंत्र शहर जो अपने आस-पास के क्षेत्र के साथ एक राज्य बनाता है)
120.example: Florence and Venice operated as independent city-states during the Renaissance.

120.english_meaning: A state in which supreme power is held by the people and their elected representatives.
120.hindi_meaning: गणराज्य (वह शासन व्यवस्था जहाँ सर्वोच्च सत्ता जनता और उसके चुने हुए प्रतिनिधियों के पास होती है)
120.example: Venice and Florence were two prominent republics in medieval Italy.

120.english_meaning: The body of all people ordained for religious duties, especially in the Christian church.
120.example: Unlike other parts of Europe, the clergy were not politically dominant in Venice.

120.english_meaning: Rulers or landowners who held power over peasants in the medieval feudal system.
120.example: Powerful feudal lords did not control the independent Italian towns.

120.english_meaning: The position or status of being a citizen of a particular country or city.
120.example: The participation of merchants in governance helped the idea of citizenship to take root.

120.english_meaning: Rulers with absolute power, typically exercised in a cruel or oppressive way.
120.example: Even under military despots, the townspeople remained proud of being citizens.

120.english_meaning: An independent country or community, especially a democratic republic.
120.example: Cardinal Gasparo Contarini wrote about the democratic government of his Venetian commonwealth.

120.english_meaning: An advisory, deliberative, or administrative body of people formally constituted.
120.example: The whole authority of the city rested in that council.

120.english_meaning: People from whom someone is descended, especially more remote than a grandparent.
120.example: Our wise ancestors ordained laws for the stability of the city.

120.english_meaning: A loud, confused noise, especially one caused by a large mass of people; public commotion.
120.example: Popular tumults often arise in cities governed directly by the common people.

120.english_meaning: Acting with or showing care and thought for the future.
120.example: Our prudent ancestors established balanced rules of governance.

120.english_meaning: The group of people belonging to the noble class in a society.
120.example: Rule of the commonwealth was defined partly by nobility of lineage.

120.english_meaning: A lineal descent from an ancestor; ancestry or pedigree.
120.example: His noble lineage allowed him a seat in the governing council.

120.english_meaning: Gave someone a noble rank or elevated status through virtue or achievement.
120.example: Citizens could also be ennobled by their virtue and service.

120.english_meaning: Full of energy and enthusiasm; pulsating with life.
120.example: Venice was one of the most vibrant and active cities in Europe.

120.english_meaning: People who sell goods, especially on a large scale or internationally.
120.example: Rich merchants and bankers actively participated in governing the city.

120.english_meaning: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or saintly interest.
120.example: The painting depicts the recovery of the relic of the Holy Cross.

120.english_meaning: Relating to or supporting democracy or its principles.
120.example: Contarini wrote about the democratic government of his city-state.

121.english_meaning: A cultural and intellectual movement that emphasized human potential, agency, and classical learning rather than strictly religious dogma.
121.hindi_meaning: मानवतावाद (वह बौद्धिक आंदोलन जो धार्मिक रूढ़ियों के बजाय मानवीय क्षमताओं और शास्त्रीय ज्ञान पर बल देता है)
121.example: Humanism encouraged scholars to study ancient Greek and Roman literature.

121.english_meaning: A title given by a government or official institution to an eminent poet.
121.example: Petrarch was given the title of Poet Laureate in Rome in 1341.

121.english_meaning: The system and technology of printing and typography that uses movable components to reproduce the elements of a document.
121.hindi_meaning: चल मुद्रण अक्षर (प्रिंटिंग के लिए अलग-अलग घूमने वाले या सजाए जाने वाले अक्षर)
121.example: Gutenberg revolutionized book production when he printed the Bible with movable type.

121.english_meaning: The measurement of distance north or south of the Equator.
121.example: Portuguese mathematicians calculated latitude by observing the sun in 1484.

121.english_meaning: A person authorized to perform legal formalities, draft contracts, and keep official records.
121.hindi_meaning: दस्तावेज लेखक / कानूनी समझौता तैयार करने वाला अधिकारी
121.example: The growing city trade created a high demand for lawyers and notaries.

121.english_meaning: The ancient past, especially the period of classical civilizations like Greece and Rome.
121.hindi_meaning: प्राचीन काल (विशेषकर यूनान और रोम की प्राचीन सभ्यता)
121.example: To Petrarch, antiquity was a distinctive civilization understood through ancient texts.

121.english_meaning: The system and structure of a language.
121.example: Humanist masters taught grammar, rhetoric, poetry, history, and moral philosophy.

121.english_meaning: The art of effective or persuasive speaking and writing.
121.hindi_meaning: वाग्मिता / प्रभावपूर्ण ढंग से बोलने या लिखने की कला
121.example: Students in universities learned rhetoric to improve their public speaking and argumentation skills.

121.english_meaning: The branch of philosophy that contemplates what is right and wrong, and human ethics.
121.example: Moral philosophy was an essential part of the humanist educational curriculum.

121.english_meaning: A Latin word used by Cicero to mean culture, refinement, and human education.
121.hindi_meaning: लातिनी शब्द 'ह्यूमनितास' (जिसका अर्थ सिसरो के अनुसार 'संस्कृति' था)
121.example: The word 'humanities' was derived from the Latin word humanitas.

121.english_meaning: A person living at the same time as another, or belonging to the same period.
121.hindi_meaning: समकालीन (एक ही काल में होने वाला व्यक्ति)
121.example: Cicero was a contemporary of Julius Caesar.

121.english_meaning: The principal church of a diocese, containing the bishop's seat.
121.example: The text compares the bustling commercial city of Venice to a traditional cathedral-town.

121.english_meaning: The activity of buying and selling, especially on a large scale.
121.example: Commerce being the chief activity in the city, there was an increasing demand for lawyers.

121.english_meaning: The stage of human social and cultural development and organization that is considered most advanced.
121.example: Petrarch viewed ancient Greece and Rome as a distinctive civilisation.

121.english_meaning: The action of explaining the meaning of something.
121.example: Notaries were needed to write and interpret rules and written agreements.

121.english_meaning: The art or practice of designing and constructing buildings.
121.example: Brunelleschi designed the magnificent Duomo in Florence.

121.english_meaning: Single; separate; focusing on personal growth and autonomous ability.
121.example: Humanist subjects emphasized skills developed by individuals through discussion and debate.

121.english_meaning: A negotiated and typically legally binding arrangement between parties.
121.example: Written agreements were crucial for conducting large-scale trade.

122.english_meaning: A thinker or scholar of the Renaissance who emphasized human potential, reason, and classical learning over strict religious dogma.
122.hindi_meaning: मानवतावादी (वह विद्वान जो मानव गरिमा, तर्क और प्राचीन शास्त्रीय ज्ञान पर बल देता है)
122.example: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola was a famous humanist of Florence.

122.english_meaning: The action or fact of achieving a goal or reaching a desired standard.
122.example: The attainment of knowledge requires consistent effort and debate.

122.english_meaning: Characterized by or involving physical or mental strength, energy, and force.
122.example: Mental energy becomes far stronger and more vigorous through intellectual debate.

122.english_meaning: Involving or causing a complete or dramatic change in ideas or methods.
122.example: These revolutionary ideas attracted attention in many universities.

122.english_meaning: In a sudden and noticeable or very great manner.
122.hindi_meaning: नाटकीय रूप से / अत्यधिक और अचानक
122.example: Things changed dramatically in Florence during the fifteenth century.

122.english_meaning: A person who is not a member of the clergy or a professional in a particular subject.
122.hindi_meaning: गृहस्थ व्यक्ति / गैर-धार्मिक व्यक्ति (जो पादरी न हो)
122.example: Dante Alighieri was a layman who wrote on religious themes.

122.english_meaning: Resembling real life; representing things accurately and naturally.
122.hindi_meaning: यथार्थवादी / जीवंत (जो बिल्कुल असली जैसा लगे)
122.example: Giotto painted lifelike portraits that differed from stiff figures of earlier artists.

122.english_meaning: Relating to the ability to think and understand things logically; mental.
122.example: Florence developed into the most exciting intellectual city in Italy.

122.english_meaning: The use of imagination or original ideas to create something; inventiveness.
122.example: The city became a vibrant centre of artistic creativity.

122.english_meaning: A person with many talents or areas of knowledge, spanning art, science, and philosophy.
122.hindi_meaning: बहुमुखी प्रतिभा संपन्न व्यक्ति (जिसे कला, विज्ञान और साहित्य कई क्षेत्रों में महारत हो)
122.example: Leonardo da Vinci is often cited as the ultimate Renaissance Man.

122.english_meaning: An expert in or student of theology (the study of religion and religious beliefs).
122.example: Many intellectuals of the era were scholar-diplomat-theologian-artist combined.

122.english_meaning: Bringing back a previous right, custom, setting, or condition; reviving.
122.example: Humanists thought they were restoring true civilisation after centuries of darkness.

122.english_meaning: A sudden and complete failure, breakdown, or fall of a structure, government, or empire.
122.example: They believed a dark age set in after the collapse of the Roman Empire.

122.english_meaning: Without asking questions or expressing doubt; accepting something as absolute truth.
122.hindi_meaning: बिना किसी संदेह के / आंख मूंदकर
122.example: Later scholars unquestioningly assumed that a new age had begun in Europe.
Scholars assumed that the medieval period was a time of darkness.

122.english_meaning: Relating to the Middle Ages (roughly from the 5th to the 15th century in European history).
122.example: The terms 'Middle Ages' and 'medieval period' are often used interchangeably.

122.english_meaning: The state or quality of being worthy of honour or respect.
122.example: Pico della Mirandola wrote extensively on the dignity of man.

122.english_meaning: An official representing a country abroad, skilled in conducting negotiations.
122.example: A Renaissance individual often functioned as a scholar, diplomat, and artist all at once.

123.english_meaning: A period of a thousand years.
123.example: A millennium has passed since the ancient city was founded.

123.english_meaning: Scholars of the Renaissance who revived the study of classical Greek and Roman art, literature, and philosophy.
123.example: The humanists believed in the importance of human potential and learning.

123.english_meaning: The process of categorizing the past into discrete, quantified blocks of time for the purpose of study.
123.hindi_meaning: काल-विभाजन (इतिहास को विभिन्न कालों में बांटना)
123.example: Historians often debate the standard periodisation of European history.
Scholars are reluctant to make sharp divisions between centuries.

123.english_meaning: Full of energy and enthusiasm; lively.
123.example: The city has a vibrant cultural life filled with art and music.

123.english_meaning: Male priests, ministers, or religious leaders in the Christian church.
123.example: Many medieval manuscripts were preserved by monks and clergymen.

123.english_meaning: Owing gratitude for a service or favor; grateful.
123.example: European scholars were deeply indebted to Arab translators.

123.english_meaning: A book or document written by hand rather than typed or printed.
123.example: Ancient manuscripts contain valuable historical knowledge.

123.english_meaning: The action or process of passing something on from one place, person, or group to another.
123.hindi_meaning: संचरण, एक जगह से दूसरी जगह पहुंचाना
123.example: The transmission of scientific knowledge took place through translations.

123.english_meaning: The branch of science which deals with celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.
123.example: Ptolemy wrote an important ancient treatise on astronomy.
The word carried a definite article in Arabic.

123.english_meaning: A qualified practitioner of medicine; a doctor.
123.example: Ibn Sina was a renowned Arab physician and philosopher.

123.english_meaning: A book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject.
123.example: Al-Razi was the author of a comprehensive medical encyclopaedia.

123.english_meaning: To settle or find a solution to a problem or contentious matter.
123.example: He tried to resolve the tension between science and belief.

123.english_meaning: The study of the nature of God and religious belief.
123.example: University curricula in the Middle Ages were heavily focused on theology.

123.english_meaning: The subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college (plural of curriculum).
123.example: School curricula were expanded to include humanist subjects.

123.english_meaning: All of the people born and living at about the same time.
123.example: Later generations misunderstood the origins of these scholars due to Europeanized spellings.

123.english_meaning: The study of the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence.
123.example: Ancient Greek philosophy greatly influenced medieval thinkers.

124.english_meaning: A person devoted to humanism, a cultural and intellectual movement that emphasized human potential, agency, and classical learning during the Renaissance.
124.hindi_meaning: मानवतावादी (वह व्यक्ति जो मनुष्य की क्षमताओं, स्वतंत्रता और शास्त्रीय ज्ञान पर बल देता है)
124.example: Humanists of the Renaissance believed in the immense potential of human intellect and creativity.

124.english_meaning: The quality or art of representing things accurately and truthfully, without idealization.
124.hindi_meaning: यथार्थवाद (चीजों को उनके वास्तविक और सजीव रूप में चित्रित करने की कला)
124.example: The shift toward realism in Renaissance art led artists to study human anatomy closely.

124.english_meaning: The branch of mathematics concerned with the properties and relations of points, lines, surfaces, and solids.
124.hindi_meaning: ज्यामिति (गणित की वह शाखा जो आकृतियों, रेखाओं और स्थानों के माप का अध्ययन करती है)
124.example: Artists used geometry to achieve accurate proportions and perspective in their paintings.

124.english_meaning: The faculty or action of forming new ideas, images, or concepts of external objects not present to the senses.
124.hindi_meaning: कल्पना शक्ति (मन में नए विचार या चित्र गढ़ने की क्षमता)
124.example: Great art requires more than just imagination; it needs careful observation of real life.

124.english_meaning: All existing matter and space considered as a whole; the cosmos.
124.example: People in the sixteenth century sought to unravel the mysteries of the world and the universe.

124.english_meaning: Small parts broken off or remaining from a larger whole.
124.hindi_meaning: अवशेष / टुकड़े (किसी बड़ी वस्तु के टूटे हुए या बचे हुए छोटे हिस्से)
124.example: Archaeologists discovered ancient fragments of art in the ruins of Rome.

124.english_meaning: The remains of a building, city, etc., that has suffered severe damage or collapse.
124.hindi_meaning: खंडहर (नष्ट या जर्जर हो चुकी इमारतों या शहरों के अवशेष)
124.example: Explorers searched the ruins of ancient cities to uncover historical treasures.

124.english_meaning: Having parts or dimensions that are properly balanced and proportioned in size and relation to each other.
124.hindi_meaning: संतुलित अनुपात वाला (जिसके अंग सही और सुंदर अनुपात में हों)
124.example: Renaissance sculptors admired the perfectly proportioned figures of classical statues.

124.english_meaning: Of a painting, statue, or description resembling real life; realistic.
124.example: Donatello created lifelike statues that revolutionized European sculpture.

124.english_meaning: The branch of science concerned with the bodily structure of humans, animals, and other living organisms.
124.hindi_meaning: शरीर रचना विज्ञान (जीवों की आंतरिक शारीरिक संरचना का अध्ययन)
124.example: Studying human anatomy allowed artists to draw muscles and bones with scientific accuracy.

124.english_meaning: Rooms or buildings equipped for scientific experiments, research, or teaching.
124.hindi_meaning: प्रयोगशालाएं (वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान या परीक्षण के लिए कक्ष)
124.example: Artists visited the laboratories of medical schools to study human bone structures.

124.english_meaning: A university academic of the highest rank.
124.hindi_meaning: प्राध्यापक / आचार्य (विश्वविद्यालय में उच्च पदस्थ शिक्षक)
124.example: Andreas Vesalius was a renowned professor of medicine at the University of Padua.

124.english_meaning: To methodically cut up a body or plant in order to study its internal parts.
124.hindi_meaning: चीरफाड़ करना / विच्छेदन करना (अध्ययन के लिए शरीर को काटना)
124.example: Andreas Vesalius was the first physician to systematically dissect the human body.

124.english_meaning: The branch of biology that deals with the normal functions of living organisms and their parts.
124.hindi_meaning: शरीरक्रिया विज्ञान (जीवों और उनके अंगों की कार्यप्रणाली का अध्ययन)
124.example: The anatomical studies during the Renaissance marked the beginning of modern physiology.

124.english_meaning: To portray, represent, or show in a picture, sculpture, or piece of writing.
124.example: Michelangelo's famous sculpture 'The Pieta' depicts Mary holding the body of Jesus.

124.english_meaning: The action or process of passing something on to others, such as ideas, knowledge, or signals.
124.hindi_meaning: संचरण / प्रसार (विचारों या ज्ञान को एक पीढ़ी से दूसरी तक पहुंचाना)
124.example: Art, architecture, and books served as powerful mediums for the transmission of humanist ideas.

124.english_meaning: The process of being mentally stimulated to do or feel something, especially to do something creative.
124.example: Renaissance artists found deep inspiration by studying the surviving works of classical antiquity.

124.english_meaning: The feeling or belief that one can rely on something or someone; a firm trust or self-assurance.
124.example: Sixteenth-century culture reflected a growing confidence in man's ability to achieve greatness.

125.english_meaning: A portrait of an artist produced or created by themselves.
125.example: This famous self-portrait is by Leonardo da Vinci.
Leonardo da Vinci had an amazing range of interests from botany and anatomy to art.

125.english_meaning: The branch of science concerned with the bodily structure of humans, animals, and other living organisms.
125.example: Study of human anatomy helped artists paint realistically.

125.english_meaning: A follower or pupil of a teacher, leader, or philosophy.
125.example: He signed his name as a disciple of experiment.

125.english_meaning: In a way that represents things in a way that is accurate to real life.
125.hindi_meaning: यथार्थवादी रूप से / वास्तविक रूप में
125.example: Painters painted the human form as realistically as possible.

125.english_meaning: The art of representing three-dimensional objects on a two-dimensional surface to give the right impression of their height, width, depth, and position.
125.example: Geometry helped artists understand perspective in painting.

125.english_meaning: Having or appearing to have length, breadth, and depth.
125.example: The play of light gave their pictures a three-dimensional quality.

125.english_meaning: The clothes worn by people in a particular period or country.
125.example: The colours and designs of costumes showed foreign influences.

125.english_meaning: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
125.example: There is evidence of the influence of Chinese and Persian art.

125.english_meaning: The attitude or practice of accepting a situation as it is and being prepared to deal with it, or an art style representing life truthfully.
125.example: The new quality in Italian art was called realism.

125.english_meaning: Restore to life or consciousness; brought back into use.
125.example: The city of Rome revived in a spectacular way in the fifteenth century.

125.english_meaning: Dug out from the ground and removed, especially to discover archaeological remains.
125.example: The ruins in Rome were carefully excavated by archaeologists.

125.english_meaning: People who study human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts.
125.example: Archaeologists carefully uncovered the ancient ruins.
